sample: Wokwi ESP32 virtual meter sends deviceId, energyConsumed, and timestamp through the API Gateway.
REST request delivered to the Ingestion Service.
Bean validation checks mandatory fields and non-negative energy; accepted payloads become Kafka energy-usage events.
Usage Service writes energy_usage points to InfluxDB and sums selected time windows; Device Service resolves ownership.
Slab forecast, device ranking, and 20% average-load standby heuristic use aggregated values.
A 10 s scheduler compares the preceding one-hour total with the configured threshold; Alert Service persists and sends the event.
Docker Engine 29.7.2 and Docker Compose v5.5.1. Java 17; Spring Boot 3.5.3 for User, Device, Ingestion, Usage, Alert, and Insight services; API Gateway uses Spring Boot 3.4.5.
React 19.2.8, Vite 8.2.2, TypeScript 6.0.2, Tailwind CSS 4.3.3, Apache Kafka 4.3.1 observed from the running container, MySQL 8.3.0, and InfluxDB 2.7.
ESP32 DevKit, potentiometer, three pushbuttons, and SSD1306 OLED simulated in Wokwi. PlatformIO IDE VS Code extension 3.3.4 and Wokwi VS Code extension 3.7.0 were used.
Four valid synthetic JSON events on 1 October 2026: 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75 kWh for analytics device 307, and 1.00 kWh for alert device 308. Fields: deviceId, energyConsumed, timestamp.
Three-day insight window; 30-day forecast horizon; fixed 10.00 charge; 0.12, 0.18, and 0.25 per-kWh slab rates; 20% standby coefficient.

One-hour aggregation window and 10 s scheduler. User 9 threshold set to 0.10 kWh for the isolated alert case. Spring AI 1.0.3 is present; Ollama CLI was not installed or used during controlled verification.

16 executed tests completed with zero failures and zero errors.
